title: Iranian operative accused of directing failed  terror plot at base US operates declares innocence and wants new lawyers | CNN Politics
text:
Source: CNN

The man accused of plotting to blow up a UK airbase where the US military operates was led out of a courtroom Thursday while shouting in Arabic after a nearly two-hour hearing devolved.

Mohammad Dawood Al-Saadi, who isaccused of directing the botched terror attackand of carrying out 18 terrorist attacks across Europe earlier this year, told a federal judge in New York through a translator that he no longer wants to be represented by court-appointed counsel and his family was trying to retain attorneys to represent him.

Al-Saadi, who US authorities say was a commander in an Iranian terrorist proxy group, said “I am an important statesman,” adding while motioning to his attorneys, “At this moment they no longer represent me.” Earlier he said he was innocent of the charges.

Al-Saadi was escorted out of the room by US Marshals after the judge repeatedly tried to shut down his speech.

When he was no longer in the courtroom, Judge Colleen McMahon told his current attorneys to tell their client his family has “an absolute right” to retain counsel. She suspended all deadlines until February to allow them time.

The hearing also focused on restrictions law enforcement has placed on Al-Saadi’s communications that he wants eased. Authorities allege — even with limitations — Al-Saadi used coded words with his family members to direct the failed attack at the UK airbasem in September. They have since cancelled phone calls with his immediate family members.

Al-Saadi’s lawyers argued the government is refusing to allow him to read religious texts in Arabic including about Imam Husayn ibn Ali, a 7th-century religious and political leader, because they describe violence.

“On its face its discriminatory,” Adam Dalack, one of his lawyers, said. He added the government won’t allow Al-Saadi to receive news reports written in Arabic from family members which he said is the only way his client can keep up on the news since he doesn’t read in English.

Al-Saadi’s lawyers said prosecutors are objecting to overseas articles that described his capture as a kidnapping. Dalack said Al-Saadi was held in an underground prison for two weeks in Turkey without contact with a lawyer or judge and was then taken to the US without extradition proceedings.

“There is a world in which you could characterize that as a kidnapping,” Dalack said.

Dalack also said he would make a motion for Al-Saadi to be treated as a military combatant who participated in the ongoing conflict between the US and Iran by plotting against a military installation.

“This is not a case for a civilian prosecution. He really should be in military custody and be released back at end of the hostility or be tried for war crimes” if warranted, Dalack said.

Prosecutor Jeffrey Coyle argued Al-Saadi is directing family members to create social media accounts to shape the narrative including calls to “crush American tails in Iraq by trampling the head of the master.”

“The problem here is the defendant has particular sway over people,” Coyle said, adding that the US is afraid people will be inspired by his statements since Al-Saadi was a high-ranking militant.

The judge observed, however, “Many criminal defendants try to shape media coverage of themselves and urge their families to do the same.” She cited Luigi Mangione, who had a cult following after he shot UnitedHealthcare’s chief executive on a Manhattan sidewalk.

“Luigi Mangione wasn’t shielded from the fact that people were outside the courthouse demonstrating in favor of him. So Mr. Al-Saadi gets to find out that there are people in Iraq that are demonstrating in favor of him. What’s the harm?” the judge asked.

The judge advised prosecutors she is likely to allow Al-Saadi to receive religious writings, but the hearing changed course after Al-Saadi told the judge he wanted different lawyers and was led out of the courtroom.

Dalack said Al-Saadi wanted to return to the Metropolitan Detention Center.
